questions.subject: essential_contacts_email
questions.prompt: The address that receives every Google notification for the organisation (a group, never a person)
questions.why: Suspension notices, security advisories and legal notices go here and nowhere else. The mailbox must exist and accept external mail; a wrong address means Google's warnings are read by nobody until the consequence arrives.
questions.pack_description: One organization-level Essential Contact, subscribed to every notification category Google routes.

questions.subject: cis_block_project_ssh_keys
questions.prompt: Block project-wide SSH keys on every instance (CIS 4.3)?
questions.why: An estate that relies on project-wide keys for break-glass access loses it the moment this is enforced, and the managed constraint is still PREVIEW with no legacy form to fall back to. Per-instance keys and OS Login keep working.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_require_shielded_vm
questions.prompt: Require Shielded VM for every new instance (CIS 4.8)?
questions.why: Not every image supports Shielded VM: an organisation with custom or older images fails instance creation until they are rebuilt — and this is the one constraint with no dry-run, so it cannot be rehearsed before it bites.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_confidential_computing
questions.prompt: Require Confidential Computing for every new instance (CIS 4.11, Level 2)?
questions.why: Confidential VMs are limited to particular machine families and cost more; enforced organisation-wide this stops most ordinary workloads from starting.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_cloud_sql_hardening
questions.prompt: Forbid public IPs and open authorized networks on Cloud SQL (CIS 6.5, 6.6)?
questions.why: Existing instances reached over a public IP lose connectivity the moment this is enforced; the private path has to exist first.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_api_key_services_dry_run
questions.prompt: Measure first: run 'API keys restricted to the services an application needs' as a DRY RUN instead of enforcing it?
questions.why: Google evaluates the rule and logs every action it would have blocked, blocking none of them, so the violation count is this organisation's own answer to whether enforcing it causes an outage. Turn this on INSTEAD of cis_api_key_services, not beside it. Nothing is enforced while it runs and the control reports as unmet, which is the truth; promote by switching this off and cis_api_key_services on.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_block_project_ssh_keys_dry_run
questions.prompt: Measure first: run 'project-wide SSH keys blocked on VM instances' as a DRY RUN instead of enforcing it?
questions.why: Google evaluates the rule and logs every action it would have blocked, blocking none of them, so the violation count is this organisation's own answer to whether enforcing it causes an outage. Turn this on INSTEAD of cis_block_project_ssh_keys, not beside it. Nothing is enforced while it runs and the control reports as unmet, which is the truth; promote by switching this off and cis_block_project_ssh_keys on.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_bucket_retention_dry_run
questions.prompt: Measure first: run 'bucket retention durations constrained organisation-wide' as a DRY RUN instead of enforcing it?
questions.why: Google evaluates the rule and logs every action it would have blocked, blocking none of them, so the violation count is this organisation's own answer to whether enforcing it causes an outage. Turn this on INSTEAD of cis_bucket_retention, not beside it. Nothing is enforced while it runs and the control reports as unmet, which is the truth; promote by switching this off and cis_bucket_retention on.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_cloud_sql_hardening_dry_run
questions.prompt: Measure first: run 'Cloud SQL public IPs and authorized networks restricted' as a DRY RUN instead of enforcing it?
questions.why: Google evaluates the rule and logs every action it would have blocked, blocking none of them, so the violation count is this organisation's own answer to whether enforcing it causes an outage. Turn this on INSTEAD of cis_cloud_sql_hardening, not beside it. Nothing is enforced while it runs and the control reports as unmet, which is the truth; promote by switching this off and cis_cloud_sql_hardening on.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.prompt: Measure first: run 'Confidential Computing required on instances' as a DRY RUN instead of enforcing it?
questions.why: Google evaluates the rule and logs every action it would have blocked, blocking none of them, so the violation count is this organisation's own answer to whether enforcing it causes an outage. Turn this on INSTEAD of cis_confidential_computing, not beside it. Nothing is enforced while it runs and the control reports as unmet, which is the truth; promote by switching this off and cis_confidential_computing on.

questions.subject: cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection_dry_run
questions.prompt: Measure first: run 'Cloud SQL IAM authentication and deletion protection required' as a DRY RUN instead of enforcing it?
questions.why: Google evaluates the rule and logs every action it would have blocked, blocking none of them, so the violation count is this organisation's own answer to whether enforcing it causes an outage. Turn this on INSTEAD of cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection, not beside it. Nothing is enforced while it runs and the control reports as unmet, which is the truth; promote by switching this off and cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection on.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_cmek_required
questions.prompt: Require customer-managed encryption keys for new resources (CIS 7.2, 7.3, 8.1)?
questions.why: The most disruptive control in the set: every new resource of a listed service must be created with a CMEK, so the key rings, the keys and the grants have to exist first — and the pack cannot know which projects may supply keys.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_api_key_services
questions.prompt: Restrict API keys to the services an application needs (CIS 4.0 §1.14 / 5.0 §1.15)?
questions.why: An API key that today calls anything stops working the moment this is enforced unless its targets are already narrowed. Set the allowed services first, then enforce.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_bucket_retention
questions.prompt: Constrain bucket retention durations organisation-wide (CIS 4.0 §2.3 / 5.0 §2.4)?
questions.why: It constrains EVERY bucket, not only the log sink's: once set, a bucket may carry a retention policy only if its duration is in the list, so buckets on other durations can no longer be updated.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_access_approval
questions.prompt: Require an approval before Google personnel reach the organisation's content (Access Approval, CIS 4.0 §2.15 / 5.0 §2.16)?
questions.why: Every support case that needs to look at the customer's content then waits for someone on the notification list to approve, and Access Transparency has to be switched on for the organisation first, in the console.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_block_internet_ssh_rdp
questions.prompt: Deny SSH and RDP from the internet across the whole organisation (CIS 3.6, 3.7)?
questions.why: On by default, because an organisation that has not closed ports 22 and 3389 to the internet is one scan away from the finding it will be asked about. A hierarchical firewall policy on the organisation is read before every VPC rule: a session reaching an instance from a PUBLIC address on either port ends the moment the policy attaches. Internal administration is not touched — the pass list carries the three private blocks as well as Google's IAP range — so what breaks is a bastion with an external IP, which needs its range listed or its access moved to IAP. Every rule logs, which is what fills the firewall half of a SIEM. Answering no is a deviation and needs a reason an auditor will read.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_cloud_sql_iam_and_deletion_protection
questions.prompt: Require IAM database authentication and deletion protection on Cloud SQL (CIS 5.0 §6.6, §6.9)?
questions.why: Every Cloud SQL create and update in the organisation must then carry both settings; tooling that creates instances without them fails, and an existing instance that lacks one is refused its next update until that update adds it.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: cis_dns_logging
questions.prompt: Require Cloud DNS policies to log queries (CIS 5.0 §2.13)?
questions.why: On by default: DNS query logs are how a compromised host asking for its command-and-control domain becomes visible, and they are small beside flow logs — one entry per query, no sampling knob. What it enforces is only half the control: a DNS policy that exists must have logging on, because no org policy can require that a network HAS a policy at all. The other half is verified live — report-compliance names the networks without one. What it breaks: creating or updating a DNS policy with logging off is refused. Answering no is a deviation and needs a reason.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: allowed_resource_locations
questions.prompt: Where may resources be created (gcp.resourceLocations)?
questions.why: Data residency is the customer's decision, not the pack's. Narrowing later refuses creation outside the list and leaves what already exists elsewhere non-compliant; widening later is what an operator once did by hand, and the next apply undid it.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: allowed_policy_member_principal_sets
questions.prompt: Which organisations' identities may be granted IAM roles (CIS §1.1, domain restricted sharing)?
questions.why: The default is the customer's own organisation. A partner organisation whose identities need roles here has to be listed, or every grant to them is refused; one listed too many opens the estate to a directory the customer does not control.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: allowed_policy_member_subjects
questions.prompt: Which individual principals may be granted roles despite the lock (Google service agents)?
questions.why: The default is Security Command Center's five organisation-level service agents, canonical and free to allow. A product whose service agent is not listed fails at the grant — Firebase Hosting, for one. Overriding REPLACES the list: keep the five when adding.
questions.pack_description: The CIS GCP Foundation 4.0 organization-policy set, managed constraints included.

questions.subject: logsink_project_id
questions.prompt: The project that holds the audit-log archive
questions.why: A project id is immutable. Changing it later creates a second project and abandons the first, with the archive bucket inside it — and every pack that points at the logging project by reference moves with it.
questions.pack_description: Organization-wide audit log sink into a GCS bucket — the compliance archive.

questions.subject: logsink_project_folder
questions.prompt: The folder the audit-archive project is created in — a folder the estate declares as `google_folder.<label>.name`, an existing one by its numeric id, or empty for the organisation
questions.why: It is the only thing that decides where the project lands. Left empty, the project is created directly under the organisation and inherits the organisation's policies and IAM alone; an estate `satz init` wrote has its infrastructure folder as `google_folder.infra_folder.name`. Changing it afterwards moves a live project between parents, which changes the policies and the grants it inherits.
questions.pack_description: Organization-wide audit log sink into a GCS bucket — the compliance archive.

questions.subject: logsink_bucket_name
questions.prompt: The archive bucket's name (globally unique)
questions.why: The bucket holds the organisation's audit history. Renaming it means a new bucket and copying the archive by hand, or losing continuity of the evidence.
questions.pack_description: Organization-wide audit log sink into a GCS bucket — the compliance archive.

questions.subject: logsink_bucket_location
questions.prompt: Where the archive bucket lives (a region or multi-region)
questions.why: A bucket's location cannot change. Audit logs are the record a regulator asks for, so where they are stored is the customer's data-residency decision, not the pack's; the default follows the estate's default region.
questions.pack_description: Organization-wide audit log sink into a GCS bucket — the compliance archive.

questions.subject: logsink_retention_days
questions.prompt: How many days the archive keeps audit logs before the lifecycle deletes them
questions.why: Shortening it later deletes everything already archived past the new age at the next lifecycle run, and there is no undo. 400 days covers a year plus the audit that follows it.
questions.pack_description: Organization-wide audit log sink into a GCS bucket — the compliance archive.

questions.subject: cis_central_email
questions.prompt: The address the organisation's security alerts are sent to (a group, never a person)
questions.why: Monitoring sends from alerting-noreply@google.com, so the mailbox must exist and accept external mail; a group whose members have no mailboxes drops every alert silently, and nothing in the estate can detect that. People leave; groups have owners.
questions.pack_description: Centralized log-based alerting for CIS 2.5-2.12 in 5.0 numbering, 2.4-2.11 in 4.0.

questions.subject: cis_central_bucket_project
questions.prompt: The project that hosts the alerting bucket, the metrics and the alert policies
questions.why: Every metric and policy is created in this project; moving them is a recreate and loses alert history. The default is the audit-logsink pack's project, by reference — one logging project for the archive and the alerting — and needs no answer beyond accepting it when that pack is used.
questions.pack_description: Centralized log-based alerting for CIS 2.5-2.12 in 5.0 numbering, 2.4-2.11 in 4.0.
